conditions.message: Chest pain with associated symptoms like sweating, nausea, or pain radiating to the left arm may indicate a heart attack. Seek emergency care immediately.
Crushing chest pain with jaw or back pain could be a heart attack. This is a medical emergency - call 911 immediately.
Sudden sharp chest pain with difficulty breathing may indicate a collapsed lung or pulmonary embolism. Seek emergency care immediately.
Sudden shortness of breath with chest pain or blue lips can indicate a life-threatening emergency such as a pulmonary embolism. Call emergency services immediately.
Severe breathing difficulty with wheezing or throat tightness may indicate anaphylaxis or severe asthma attack. Use emergency inhaler/epinephrine and call 911.
Breathing difficulty with facial or tongue swelling indicates severe allergic reaction. Use epinephrine auto-injector if available and call 911 immediately.
A sudden, severe headache with confusion, stiff neck, or loss of consciousness may suggest a brain bleed or meningitis. Seek emergency care immediately.
The worst headache of your life with sudden onset (thunderclap headache) may indicate brain hemorrhage. Call 911 immediately.
Severe headache with fever, neck stiffness, and light sensitivity may indicate meningitis. Seek emergency care immediately.
Headache after head injury with confusion or vomiting may indicate serious brain injury. Go to emergency room immediately.
Severe abdominal pain with fever, persistent vomiting, or blood in the stool could indicate appendicitis or other serious conditions. Get urgent medical evaluation.
Severe abdominal pain with rigid, distended abdomen may indicate bowel obstruction or perforation. Seek emergency care immediately.
Severe right upper abdominal pain with jaundice and fever may indicate gallbladder infection or bile duct obstruction. Seek urgent medical care.
Severe abdominal/flank pain with blood in urine may indicate kidney stones or kidney infection. Seek urgent medical evaluation.
Sudden weakness, facial drooping, or slurred speech are signs of stroke. Time is critical - call 911 immediately. Note the time symptoms started.
First-time seizure or prolonged seizure requires immediate emergency evaluation. Call 911.
Sudden severe confusion or altered mental state may indicate serious medical emergency (infection, stroke, metabolic crisis). Seek emergency care immediately.
Sudden vision changes with muscle weakness may indicate serious neurological condition. Seek immediate medical evaluation.
Uncontrolled bleeding or severe blood loss is a medical emergency. Apply direct pressure and call 911 immediately.
Vomiting blood or coffee-ground material indicates serious internal bleeding. Seek emergency care immediately.
Black tarry stools or large amounts of blood in stool with dizziness indicates serious gastrointestinal bleeding. Go to emergency room immediately.
Coughing up blood, especially in large amounts, requires immediate emergency evaluation. Call 911.
A rash with sudden swelling or breathing difficulty may indicate a severe allergic reaction (anaphylaxis). Use an epinephrine auto-injector if available and call emergency services immediately.
Purple non-blanching rash with fever and stiff neck may indicate meningococcal meningitis. This is a life-threatening emergency - call 911 immediately.
Severe blistering rash with peeling skin and fever may indicate Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis. Seek emergency care immediately.
Dizziness with sudden weakness, speech problems, or vision changes may be signs of a stroke. Call emergency services immediately.
Dizziness with fainting and chest pain may indicate heart rhythm problems. Seek emergency evaluation immediately.
Dizziness with severe headache and confusion may indicate serious neurological emergency. Call 911.
Fever with stiff neck, confusion, or seizures may indicate meningitis or a severe systemic infection. Seek emergency care immediately.
Very high fever (>103°F/39.4°C) with breathing difficulty or chest pain requires emergency evaluation.
Fever after travel to tropical areas with severe symptoms may indicate serious infection like malaria or dengue. Seek immediate medical care.
Any fever in immunocompromised patients requires urgent medical evaluation. Contact your oncologist or go to emergency room.
Severe abdominal pain or heavy bleeding during pregnancy could indicate miscarriage or ectopic pregnancy. Seek emergency care immediately.
Severe headache with vision changes and swelling in pregnancy may indicate preeclampsia/eclampsia. This is life-threatening - go to emergency room immediately.
Decreased or absent fetal movement requires immediate evaluation. Go to labor and delivery or emergency room.
Water breaking before 37 weeks (preterm premature rupture of membranes) requires immediate obstetric evaluation.
Seizures during pregnancy (eclampsia) is a life-threatening emergency. Call 911 immediately.
Sudden confusion, seizures, or loss of consciousness may indicate a serious neurological or systemic emergency. Call emergency services immediately.
Suicidal thoughts or intent to harm self or others requires immediate psychiatric emergency evaluation. Call 911 or crisis hotline.
Active suicidal ideation with plan is a psychiatric emergency. Call National Suicide Prevention Lifeline (988) or 911 immediately.
Fever in infant under 3 months old requires immediate emergency evaluation. Go to emergency room or call pediatrician immediately.
Severe breathing difficulty in child with blue lips or retractions is a medical emergency. Call 911 immediately.
Signs of severe dehydration in infant/child (no urine, sunken soft spot) require urgent medical evaluation.
Allergic reaction with breathing difficulty in child requires immediate epinephrine and emergency care. Call 911.
Head injury in child with loss of consciousness or persistent vomiting requires emergency evaluation.
Poison ingestion or medication overdose in child requires immediate action. Call Poison Control (1-800-222-1222) and 911.
Severe bleeding with spurting blood indicates arterial bleeding. Apply direct pressure and call 911 immediately.
Head injury with loss of consciousness requires immediate emergency evaluation for possible traumatic brain injury. Call 911.
Suspected spinal injury - DO NOT MOVE the person. Call 911 and keep them still until emergency services arrive.
Open fracture with bone protruding through skin is a medical emergency. Call 911 and do not attempt to move the limb.
Severe burns, especially on face/airway or from electricity, require immediate emergency care. Call 911.
Penetrating injury to chest or abdomen - DO NOT remove embedded object. Call 911 immediately.
Sudden vision loss or curtain over vision may indicate retinal detachment. Seek emergency ophthalmology care immediately.
Chemical exposure to eye requires immediate flushing with water for 15 minutes, then emergency care. Call 911 while flushing.
Severe eye pain with halos around lights may indicate acute angle-closure glaucoma. Seek emergency ophthalmology care immediately to prevent permanent vision loss.
Penetrating eye injury - do NOT remove object or apply pressure. Cover loosely and go to emergency room immediately.
Very high blood sugar with confusion and rapid breathing may indicate diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA). This is life-threatening - go to emergency room immediately.
Severe low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) with confusion or unconsciousness requires immediate treatment. Give glucose if conscious, call 911 if unconscious.
Choking with inability to speak or breathe requires immediate Heimlich maneuver and call 911.
Severe asthma attack not responding to inhaler or with blue lips requires emergency care. Call 911 and continue using rescue inhaler.
Sudden severe chest pain with extreme shortness of breath may indicate collapsed lung (pneumothorax). Seek emergency care immediately.
Cardiac arrest - person unresponsive and not breathing. Call 911 immediately and start CPR. Use AED if available.
Severe heart palpitations with chest pain or fainting may indicate dangerous arrhythmia. Seek emergency care immediately.
Anaphylaxis is a life-threatening allergic reaction. Use epinephrine auto-injector immediately and call 911. Do not wait to see if symptoms improve.
Severe reaction to insect sting with breathing difficulty or widespread swelling requires emergency care and epinephrine.
Absence of urine output with swelling and confusion may indicate acute kidney failure. Seek emergency care immediately.
Severe flank pain with fever and blood in urine may indicate kidney infection or obstruction. Seek urgent medical care.
Severe dehydration with confusion and rapid heartbeat requires emergency IV fluids. Go to emergency room immediately.
Thyroid storm (severe hyperthyroidism) with rapid heart rate, fever, and confusion is life-threatening. Call 911 immediately.
Signs of sepsis (severe infection) including fever, confusion, and rapid breathing are life-threatening. Go to emergency room immediately.
Rapidly spreading skin infection with severe pain may indicate necrotizing fasciitis (flesh-eating bacteria). This is a surgical emergency - call 911.
